safe_temperature.temperature: 165°F (73.9°C) measured in the thickest part of the breast and innermost thigh without touching bone

source.name: SAFE MINIMUM INTERNAL TEMPERATURES as measured with a food thermometer - FDA & USDA Guidelines

safe_temperature.disagreements: There is zero disagreement across FDA, USDA, and notebook culinary sources that all chicken parts, whole birds, and ground poultry must reach a minimum internal temperature of 165°F (73.9°C) for food safety. However, culinary sources note important cut-specific texture optimization: lean breast meat should be pulled right at 165°F because cooking past that temperature rapidly expels moisture and leaves meat stringy and chalky; conversely, dark meat (thighs, drumsticks, wings) contains more fat and connective tissue and is significantly more succulent, tender, and flavorful when cooked to 175°F–180°F (79°C–82°C).

methods.time: 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes (approx. 18 to 20 minutes per pound)
methods.doneness: Internal temperature reaches 165°F in deepest part of thigh and breast; juices run clear with no pink; skin is deeply golden and blistered
methods.rest: 10 to 15 minutes tented loosely with foil before carving
methods.tips: Pat chicken bone-dry inside and out with paper towels; rub butter or oil both under and over the skin; season cavity generously and insert aromatics (halved lemon, garlic head, fresh rosemary sprigs); do not tie legs too tightly so heat circulates freely around inner thigh joints.

source.name: How To Roast a Whole Chicken - Garden in the Kitchen & Epicurious 101

methods.cut: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs or drumsticks
methods.doneness: Internal temperature reaches 175°F–180°F for optimal tenderness; skin is deeply golden, crispy, and crackling
methods.tips: Place thighs skin-side up on a rimmed baking sheet with space between pieces; high heat renders the fat cap beneath the skin, creating a self-basting crispy exterior without requiring breading.

source.name: Baked Chicken Thighs (Crispy and Juicy!) | Downshiftology

methods.cut: boneless, skinless chicken breasts (pounded or butterflied to even 3/4-inch thickness)
methods.heat: Medium-high heat in heavy cast-iron skillet with oil and butter
methods.time: 4 to 6 minutes on first side, flip, and 3 to 4 minutes on second side (approx. 8 to 10 minutes total)
methods.doneness: Internal temperature hits exactly 165°F; flesh is springy to the touch and juices run clear
methods.rest: 3 to 5 minutes on a warm plate before carving (never slice immediately)
methods.tips: Pound breasts to uniform thickness so tapered ends do not dry out before the thick center cooks; pat completely dry; let sear undisturbed to build a golden crust; baste with foaming butter, garlic, and herbs during the final 2 minutes.

source.name: The Best Chicken Breast You'll Ever Make | Epicurious 101 & A Couple Cooks

methods.cut: chicken breast tenders, cutlets, or bone-in pieces
methods.doneness: Coating is crunchy and golden-brown; reaches 165°F internal temperature
methods.tips: Lightly spray air fryer basket with oil; arrange chicken in a single uncrowded layer; a light spritz of oil over breadcrumbs ensures a golden crunch without deep frying.

methods.cut: boneless breasts, bone-in thighs, or chicken skewers
methods.time: 5 to 7 minutes per side for boneless breasts; 8 to 10 minutes per side for bone-in thighs
methods.doneness: 165°F internal temperature; juices run clear with distinct grill marks
methods.tips: Marinate in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and fresh rosemary for 15 to 30 minutes; clean and oil grates thoroughly; keep grill lid closed to maintain ambient roasting heat.

methods.heat: Medium-high heat to brown, then low heat covered simmer

methods.tips: Brown skin-on chicken pieces first in skillet to build foundational fond, remove, cook aromatics and vegetables, return chicken and simmer partially submerged in broth, tomatoes, or wine.

avoid.warning: Washing raw chicken under running tap water: splashes Campylobacter, Salmonella, and other pathogens up to 3 feet across countertops, sinks, and utensils.
Undercooking poultry below 165°F: raw or undercooked chicken presents significant bacterial food safety hazards; verify with a thermometer in thickest part of breast and thigh.
Overcooking lean chicken breast meat past 165°F: lean breast meat contains minimal fat; cooking past 165°F rapidly dries out the protein fibers, leaving meat tough and stringy.
Carving chicken immediately off heat: slicing without resting causes internal juices to pool out onto the cutting board; rest whole bird 10-15 minutes and breasts 3-5 minutes.
